speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health whether the Ministry will consider allowing children under the age of 18 to access Tier 2 low-intensity services such as counselling or screening by licensed practitioners, without parental consent, while retaining the requirement for parental consent for higher-risk interventions such as medication or hospitalisation.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry can provide an update regarding the study of the requirement for parental consent for children and young people below 18 or 21 to access mental health support; (b) which stakeholders have been engaged; (c) when is the study expected to be completed; and (d) whether the findings will be made public.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: However, it is generally good practice for parents to be involved when mental health services are provided to young people.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Part of the reason is that parents play a vital role in supporting their children’s well-being and their involvement in their children’s recovery journey is critical.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There has been feedback that the requirement of parental consent is one of the reasons why young people with mental health challenges hesitate to seek help.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Indeed, the issue of requiring parental consent before seeking help and involving parents as part of the recovery journey, need not be conflated.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Key stakeholders including parents, youths and service providers were engaged, and their views will contribute towards shaping the guidelines.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: The Senior Minister of State spoke about emotional support.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: We are actually asking about the Tier 2 low-intensity services such as counselling by licensed practitioners.

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: And then, does the Ministry have a clearer timeline on when the update will be and will the findings be made public on this review?

speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
text: I would also like to check with the Senior Minister of State, if there is no prescription on age, from my understanding working with the social service agencies, they also tend to feel that the requirement for this is quote opaque and wish to know what is the direction that MOH will take.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As Members can understand, this is a process that requires us to engage stakeholders and understand from their perspectives what would be helpful and what would be more of a deterrent.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we will do this work seriously and put up something, hopefully, by some time early next year.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In terms of the different situations in which services need to be provided and how caregivers, including counsellors and social service agencies, can navigate this space and be clear about what kinds of roles they can play, I think what we will do is to provide these guidelines which will give a framework where the service providers be better guided in assessing the situations in which minors seek mental health support.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: While I said earlier that parental support is a preferred approach for some of these services to be delivered, the guidelines do recognise that there may be specific circumstances in which requiring parental consent would deter a minor from seeking the help that they need.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is a balance that we need to strike.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On the one hand, we want parental involvement, but sometimes, for the situation in which the minors are seeking help, it could be linked to their relationship with their parents as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we do need to take a very sensitive approach to this.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And I hope the guidelines and framework will give the service providers better clarity on how to navigate this space and be sensitive to the needs of both parents and children.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I am asking this in the capacity as a member of the People's Action Party Mental Health Group.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: In my interactions with the social service agencies, one of them raised this concern: how do we ensure that those that are below 18, that as long as they are below 18, that this will be adopted?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Meaning that if they are below 18, no parental consent will be needed.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: So, from the social service agencies' perspective, they do not need to reach out for parents to get their consent?
